name: Sparse Autoencoders for Gemma-4-E4B-it
description: Trained and published sparse autoencoders for the instruction-tuned google/gemma-4-E4B-it after discovering that the official base-model SAEs fail catastrophically on its activations (held-out variance explained below zero at every layer). Warm-starting from the base SAEs and continue-training ~25M tokens per layer on a mix of pile and chat-template data recovers them to VE ≈ 0.81–0.87 at the original sparsity (L0 ≈ 100). Three matryoshka batch-topk SAEs (layers 7/21/35, 65,536 features each) released on HuggingFace in sae_lens format, with a model card documenting an evaluation-methodology finding: 0.1% of tokens can carry over half the reconstruction error, so short-text evals dramatically overstate SAE health.

name: Macaulay2 Internals Dev
description: A set of developer-facing resources for exploring the internals of the Macaulay2 computer algebra system, built for the Building the Future of Macaulay2 workshop at Georgia Tech. They include an interactive explorer of Macaulay2's C++ engine — a tree view of implementation boundaries and a top-down workspace map of its subsystems — alongside a visual guide to the engine and full Doxygen-generated API documentation, to help new contributors navigate and extend the core codebase.

name: KnotMosaics Package for SageMath
description: A SageMath package for constructing, visualizing, and analyzing knot mosaic diagrams. Represents an n-mosaic as a matrix of standard tile labels and implements the local connectivity rules needed to validate mosaics, trace strands and components, compute planar diagram codes, generate random examples, and construct rational tangle mosaics. The planar diagram interface bridges mosaic representations to existing knot and link software (e.g. for computing Jones polynomials or knot Floer homology checks). Submitted upstream to SageMath as PR #42157.

name: Volatility Complex
description: A pipeline for topological analysis of S&P 500 sector volatility using Vietoris-Rips complexes and persistent homology. Computes rolling volatility correlations from log-returns, converts them to a correlation-based distance metric, and builds time-varying simplicial complexes whose evolution reveals market regime structure — dense complexes during periods of stress, fragmented clusters during calm regimes — while tracking multi-scale topological features via filtration. Built as the capstone project for the Erdős Institute Quantitative Finance Bootcamp.

name: Steering
description: A local interpretability workbench for live SAE feature steering in TransformerLens models. Built at OpenAI's Bellevue Codex Hackathon, it combines a FastAPI web UI, CLI, Textual TUI, SAE Lens hooks, and Neuronpedia label caching to compare baseline and steered GPT-2 small continuations from identical prompts.

name: Neural Network Elements
description: An interactive web-based tool for analyzing the geometry of ReLU neural networks. Computes polyhedral decompositions of the input space, constructs dual graphs of activation regions, performs spectral analysis via Laplacian eigendecomposition, and visualizes decision boundaries — all in the browser, with no server required. Approximately 4,200 lines of code, released by the Georgia Tech Research Institute.

name: KnotAI
description: A PyTorch feedforward neural network classifier for recognizing and classifying knots from their matrix (mosaic) representations. Built as part of the Washington eXperimental Mathematics Lab (WXML) project "Teaching a Computer to Knot," this model encodes knot diagrams as structured matrices and trains a graph neural network to predict knot invariants and knot types.

name: Discrete Gradients in SageMath
description: A SageMath library for computing discrete gradient vector fields on simplicial complexes via Morse theory. Implements algorithms for constructing and analyzing discrete Morse functions, computing Laplacian eigendecompositions, and extracting topological features. Released as companion code for the Annals of Combinatorics publication (2023).

name: A¹-Brouwer Degrees in Macaulay2
description: An official Macaulay2 package for computing A¹-Brouwer degrees, local and global Grothendieck–Witt invariants, and related enumerative signatures over arbitrary fields. Developed collaboratively and published in the Journal of Software for Algebra and Geometry (2024). The package is distributed with Macaulay2 as part of its standard library.
